questions.question: In a full-rank lattice L(B) in R^n, what does det(L) = |det(B)| represent?
options: The volume of the fundamental parallelepiped (covolume)
The length of a shortest non-zero lattice vector (λ1)
The count of lattice points inside one fundamental cell
The average squared length of the basis vectors in B
questions.explanation: For full rank, |det(B)| is the volume of the fundamental parallelepiped, and it is a lattice invariant (covolume).

questions.question: Which property defines a unimodular integer matrix U?
options: It has integer entries and determinant equal to ±1
It has integer entries and determinant equal to 0
It has real entries and determinant equal to 1
It has orthonormal columns and determinant equal to 1
questions.explanation: Unimodular means det(U)=±1 with integer entries, so U maps Z^n bijectively to itself.

questions.question: If U is unimodular, which statement is always true about L(B) and L(BU)?
options: They generate the same lattice set: L(B) = L(BU)
They always have identical basis vector lengths and angles
They always have identical Gram–Schmidt coefficients for B
They always have the same column vectors in the same order
questions.explanation: Unimodular changes are just a change of integer coordinates, so the set {Bz : z∈Z^n} stays the same.

questions.question: Which identity correctly relates det(BU), det(B), and det(U) for square matrices?
options: |det(BU)| = |det(B)|·|det(U)|
|det(BU)| = |det(B)| + |det(U)|
|det(BU)| = |det(B)| / |det(U)|
|det(BU)| = |det(U)| - |det(B)|
questions.explanation: Determinants multiply: det(BU)=det(B)det(U). Taking absolute values gives the covolume relation.

questions.question: What does the second successive minimum λ2(L) mean (Euclidean norm)?
options: Smallest radius containing two independent lattice vectors
Smallest radius containing two distinct lattice points
Smallest radius containing the full fundamental parallelepiped
Smallest radius containing two vectors from one chosen basis
questions.explanation: λ2 is the smallest radius r such that the lattice contains two linearly independent vectors of norm ≤ r.

questions.question: Why can brute-forcing z in a window [-k,k]^n miss the true λ1 if k is too small?
options: Short vector may require coefficients outside the window [-k,k]^n
Determinant changes under unimodular basis changes of B
The Euclidean norm depends on the order you list basis vectors
All lattices have infinitely many distinct shortest vectors
questions.explanation: A short lattice vector might be a combination with large coefficients in a skewed basis, so a small window can miss it.

questions.question: Two 2D lattices have bases diag(1,100) and diag(10,10). Which statement is correct?
options: Both determinants are 100, but λ1 differs: 1 vs 10
Both determinants are 100, and λ1 is 10 for both lattices
Determinants differ, but λ1 is 10 for both lattices
Determinants differ, and λ1 is 1 for both lattices
questions.explanation: Both lattices have the same covolume (100), but the shortest vector length depends on the geometry, not just the volume.

questions.question: For the 2D basis b1=(2,0), b2=(1,1) (as columns), what is det(L)?
questions.explanation: With columns b1,b2, the matrix is [[2,1],[0,1]] and its determinant is 2.
